acceptance_gate: Gate sees just the eight initial labels, is frozen on structurally disjoint rules, and every held arm has the same public on-demand program and verified-column caching facilities.
completion_gate: Replay exact outputs and common feedback for the entire preselected stream and report the first prefix with fully charged payback or the measured terminal cost gap.
objective: Fit a decision about one optional fold attempt from early examples on separate rules, freeze it, and compare cumulative cost against median search on a preselected longer stream under matched feedback and on-demand cache access.
status: No break-even in 32,768 held rules or any repeat. The fitted gate chose ordinary median for every prefix. Full costs including original fold and gate training were 31.065 s versus 12.403 s, a remaining gap of 18.662 s. Independent exhaustive circuit and prefix-cost replay passed.
stop_rule: Finish every rule in the bound stream in every arm; do not truncate at crossing or revise the threshold after any held result.
title: When does an example-guided fold repay learning and verification?
